hints.title: Two-Transaction Boundary Cap Obstacle
hints.text: You may complete at most two transactions, meaning you must sell the first share before buying the second. How can tracking the net balance after each sequential buy and sell step model the optimal two trades?

hints.title: Four Sequential State Invariant
hints.text: Maintain four states: buy1 (max profit after first buy), sell1 (max profit after first sell), buy2 (max profit after second buy), and sell2 (max profit after second sell).

hints.title: Four Scalar State Transition Procedure
hints.text: Initialize buy1 = -infinity, sell1 = 0, buy2 = -infinity, sell2 = 0. For each price p in prices, sequentially update buy1 = max(buy1, -p), sell1 = max(sell1, buy1 + p), buy2 = max(buy2, sell1 - p), and sell2 = max(sell2, buy2 + p). Return sell2.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxProfit(self, prices: List[int]) -> int:
        buy1, sell1 = float('-inf'), 0
        buy2, sell2 = float('-inf'), 0
        for p in prices:
            buy1 = max(buy1, -p)
            sell1 = max(sell1, buy1 + p)
            buy2 = max(buy2, sell1 - p)
            sell2 = max(sell2, buy2 + p)
        return sell2
```

variables: N: number of days in prices
complexity.notes: Single pass updates four scalar transaction registers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching all pairs of non-overlapping buy-sell intervals takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Tracking the 4 successive trading states (buy1, sell1, buy2, sell2) in constant space.
